question.prompt: Each principal of Lincoln High School serves exactly one \(3\)-year term. What is the maximum number of principals this school could have during an \(8\)-year period?

solutions.explanation:
Interpret the principals' terms as successive and nonoverlapping. An \(8\)-year period can include the end of one principal's term and the beginning of another's.

If five principals served during the period, the middle three would each have their entire \(3\)-year term inside it. Those terms alone would require \(3\cdot3=9\) years, so five principals are impossible.

Four are possible: take the last \(1\) year of one term, two complete \(3\)-year terms, and the first \(1\) year of the next term. These portions total
\[
1+3+3+1=8\text{ years}.
\]
The maximum is therefore \(4\) principals, choice C.
solutions.title: Allow partial terms at both ends
